Bringing together sculpture, drawing and live action, the exhibition will take the form of an immersive installation. Made in collaboration with LGBTQIA+ communities in and around Manchester, Vitalities explores queer grief and houses, amongst other artworks, eight luminescent sculptures created in workshops with people who have experienced grief as a process of reflection and catharsis. Witches and Healers draws on Rosie Reed Hillman’s groundbreaking project Something That Was Ours and explores what it means to be a witch today. Themes explored include wellbeing, aging and place in relation to magic, healing and ritual offering an unparalleled insight into the diverse lives of women who live as witches and healers. Through a feminist lens Hillman uses a mixture of moving image and photography to explore menopause, mental health, outsider identities and sisterhood as well as how women imagine a better world through ritual and magic. Completely free to attend and running until February 2027, drop by to see the exhibition or book in for one of the accompanying workshops or film screenings throughout its run. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. A-Kin founded by long-time friends Gasim and Sean, have become one of the city’s most exciting supper club names, turning dinners into nights built around food, music and conversation. Portfolio brings Julian Pizer back to the grills Tartuffe , as ever, will be holding the whole thing together from the grills, starting with oysters and venison, bringing in a seasonal nectarine gazpacho, and finishing their side of the menu with Alp Blossom cheese and elderberry honey before Kallos take things into dessert Tartuffe start things off with an oyster dressed with beef fat, wasabi and XO. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Join this creative workshop for some stitching, chatting, and sharing inspired by the museum’s collections This year marks 100 years since the 1926 General Strike – when almost two million people walked out on strike across the country. In this workshop, participants will learn more about this extraordinary act of solidarity, discuss the factors that caused it, and reflect on its lega Participants will then create textiles inspired by the discussions, which will be used as part of a collective textile piece responding to the On The Line: 100 years of strikes & solidarity exhibition (until Mon 2 November 2026) Part of PHM’s programme of activity exploring the history of strikes and solidarity Suitable for 12+ (under 16s must have an accompanying adult) If you require British Sign Language (BSL) interpretation please contact access@phm.org.uk or 0161 838 9190

Witches and Healers draws on Rosie Reed Hillman’s groundbreaking project Something That Was Ours and explores what it means to be a witch today. Themes explored include wellbeing, aging and place in relation to magic, healing and ritual offering an unparalleled insight into the diverse lives of women who live as witches and healers. Through a feminist lens Hillman uses a mixture of moving image and photography to explore menopause, mental health, outsider identities and sisterhood as well as how women imagine a better world through ritual and magic. Completely free to attend and running until February 2027, drop by to see the exhibition or book in for one of the accompanying workshops or film screenings throughout its run. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Residents from across Stockport have helped create SUBTEXT, which opens at Stockroom on 15 October 2026 as part of the National Year of Reading The exhibition looks at the stories, memories and ideas behind the words we read, from favourite books and personal memories to the different ways people connect with reading in everyday life It follows a series of creative workshops with local residents, led by international artist and filmmaker Parham Ghalamdar. During the workshops, people shared quotes from books, memories and ideas, helping to shape a new film-based artwork: Subtitles for a Film That Does Not Yet Parham Ghalamdar is an Iranian artist and filmmaker based in the UK whose work includes film, painting, ceramics and writing. His practice often brings words and images together to explore memory, storytelling and shared experiences, which are at the heart of SUBTEXT Cllr Dan Oliver, Cabinet Member for Communities, Culture and Public Protection at Stockport Council, said: “Stockroom is all about opening up culture, creativity and learning for people across Stockport, so it is fantastic to see local people playing such an important part in sha “SUBTEXT is a great example of how local voices, stories and experiences can help create something new. I hope it inspires people to come along, explore the exhibition and see how reading and creativity can bring people together in different ways.”

The eFalls pilot, launched in Wigan in February 2025, used routine NHS data to identify more than 1,100 people aged 65 and over who were at increased risk of falling in the following year.. . People identified through the pilot were contacted through their GP practice and invited for a health check, with support offered to help reduce their risk of falling.. . Almost eight in 10 people offered support chose to take part, with many going on to attend local strength and balance classes through the Falls Management Exercise (FaME) programme.. . The evaluation found that the benefits of taking part went beyond helping people improve their balance.. . Participants reported feeling stronger when getting up from a chair and walking outside, as well as having greater confidence to go out alone and less worry about falling.. . Some people also reported sleeping better, feeling brighter and enjoying being active again. They said they found it "very difficult to accept" Papyrus was closing Chair of Papyrus trustees Harry Biggs-Davison said: "It has been almost unbearable for us trustees to have had to make the decision." Biggs-Davison, who lost his 25-year-old son Patrick to suicide, in 2015 said he took pride "in the certainty that our charity has saved and offered hope to countless young lives during the past 30 years" But he added: "After nearly two years of struggling to keep the charity alive in such a difficult financial climate, we have had to accept that we have no alternative."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A long-running legal battle over public loans worth £140m made by Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) to a city centre developer could be heading to the Supreme Court Landowner Aubrey Weis has applied for permission to appeal against the GMCA in the ongoing dispute over loans to so-called "special purpose vehicles" - companies set up to deliver specific development projects - linked to Renaker founder Daren Whitaker The application follows attempts to overturn the earlier ruling in hearings to the Competition Appeal Tribunal and the Court of Appeal Weis's lawyers claim the loans were unfair subsidies, but the Court of Appeal ruling in June found there had been "no error of law" in the GMCA's decision to provide them Lawyers representing Weis argued earlier this year that loans made by the GMCA to Renaker were made on a "flawed and unlawful" basis and offered "unduly favourable" interest rates The funding came from the Greater Manchester Housing Investment Loans Fund (GMHILF) and supported the Trinity Islands and New Jackson developments in Manchester city centre

Revnu was founded by George Jefferson and Art Freebrey, who first met in secondary school before going on to launch a string of businesses together while still in education. Their early ventures included software to automate the buying and selling of rare vintage clothes and trainers, before they went on to build an accounting platform for Vinted sellers. While at university, their businesses were generating around $15,000 a month. After recognising that the AI systems they had developed to automate work in their own businesses could have a much wider application, George and Art were encouraged by Monzo co-founder Jonas Templestein to pursue the opportunity and apply to Y Combinator. The pair then dropped out of university and moved temporarily to Silicon Valley to take part in the renowned accelerator. Revnu has now raised $3m in a round led by NPIF II – PXN Equity Finance, which is managed by PXN Ventures as part of the Northern Powerhouse Investment Fund II. The company also received backing from Y Combinator. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester AI firm reaches £13m ARR - without a sales team Posted on September 21, 2026 by staff Manchester AI firm reaches £13m ARR – without a sales team Saber, founded by two engineers after a single audit job, now automates correspondence and document work for regulated firms Share: Founders A Manchester-based AI-native company that streamlines operational workflows has passed five million cases processed for regulated firms in under three years – built entirely without a sales team, marketing function or paid acquisition. Saber was founded in January 2024 by Jakub Lenski and Mitchel Shephard after completing a one-off audit for a law firm. Tasked with auditing a 200,000-claim book by hand – a job estimated to take six weeks to complete 10% of – Saber produced a one-off automation workflow that processed the entire book in under three days. Saber has since evolved into a Manchester team of 32 – mostly engineers – and a product that saves 96.3% of time per case. Concerns over AI’s accuracy can be a barrier to adoption, making human oversight a key component of Saber’s design. At a time when 42% of companies abandon most AI initiatives before production, Saber goes live on a real production workflow in approximately two weeks and provides measurable return on investment right from deployment. Lenski puts that down to how the software gets deployed rather than the models themselves. “Most automation projects in regulated sectors take six months to go live,” said Lenski. “By then the workflow has moved on, the team has lost faith, and the original business case is unrecognisable. “We built Saber so the platform is live on a real production workflow within two weeks – and the customer proves the savings on their own data before signing anything commercial.” VCs back InTo

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester’s Sister and Dublin’s Guinness Enterprise Centre Sign MoU Partnership to Accelerate UK-Irish Startup Growth - Invest Manchester Skip to main content Skip to footer Creative & media , Digital, cyber & AI , Life sciences & healthcare innovation , Place Manchester’s Sister and Dublin’s Guinness Enterprise Centre Sign MoU Partnership to Accelerate UK-Irish Startup Growth Published on September 23, 2026 News Sister, Manchester’s £1.7bn innovation district, and Guinness Enterprise Centre (GEC) , a world-leading incubation space for startups based in Dublin, Ireland, have signed a 12-month Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to help local startups scale overseas. The partnership aims to lower entry barriers for scaling businesses by providing reciprocal workspace access, market entry support, and cross-border network integration across two of Europe’s most dynamic technology hubs. Building on the 2025 Liverpool City Region and Greater Manchester Trade Mission in Dublin, the partnership aims to unlock cross-border commercial potential, strengthening the £2bn Manchester–Dublin corridor by creating clear international expansion pathways for early-stage businesses. Earlier this year, the airline announced it would launch flights from the UK to Lapland in December, offering five new routes to Kuusamo in Finnish Lapland from European airports, including services from Lond By the end of 2026 the airline plans to reduce its fleet from 54 aircraft to 36, while some staff members may also lose their jobs. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts The Apple Watch text that changed a family's life forever "All I have left of the last 20 years of my life is her" View 4 Images Clair Fitzharris and son Sam Fitzharris (Image: Greater Manchester Police) Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 05:59, 09 Oct 2026 It was a drizzly, cold afternoon on December 23, 2023. Martin Fitzharris was busy building his nephew a PC for Christmas . He was expecting his partner, Clair Fitzharris, son, Sam, and 13-year-old daughter Instead, he received a text that changed his life forever. Clair's Apple Watch, which had him as a named emergency contact, sent him a message to say they had been involved in a collision Within seconds of getting that text he relentlessly tried to call each of them who had been in that car that afternoon, with no success. Eventually someone answered Clair's phone, but it wasn't Clair It was sadly too late. Clair, 42, and Sam, 15, had been killed . His daughter had been left with life-changing injuries that still require surgery to this day Manchester's Minshull Street Crown Court heard that Andrew Hall had collided with their Nissan on Ripponden Road, Oldham , after veering onto the opposite side of the road. He had been travelling at over 90mph, and overtaken over cards, and braked three seconds before the crash

Greater Manchester’s new mayor spoke of how Middletonians had felt forgotten for too long – and promised her backing for regeneration, with local opinions at its heart She took to the stage alongside actor and comedian Steve Coogan, CEO of Co-operatives UK Rose Marley and Rochdale council leader Neil Emmott to push forward the Middleton Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC) This aims to bring Metrolink trams to Middleton; create new homes on brownfield plots; build high-quality business premises; and better public areas, roads and pathways “It’s what people actually want to see,” Ms Craig told Middleton Arena. “It’s about doing things in a collective way. A £6 oat milk latte isn’t the sign of regeneration.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Bolton council meeting descends into chaos as public gallery cleared and councillors walk out The meeting, which was held on the October 7 anniversary of the deadly Hamas attacks on Israel, heard a request for the Palestinian flag to flown in B A chaotic council meeting in Bolton saw the public gallery cleared after disruption and a walk out by several councillors as a request to fly the Palestinian flag on the town’s library was brought forward The agenda of the full council meeting included a question from Rumworth Green Party councillor Ismail Ibrahim, who asked for the Palestinian flag to be flown above Bolton Central library on Sunday, November 15, which is Palestinian independence day He also requested a short civic ceremony open to people of all faiths and none The council meeting took place on October 7, the third anniversary of the Hamas attacks on Israel during which around 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken as hostage Leader of the council Akhtar Zaman said raising the issue on October 7 ‘would be seen by many as inappropriate’

He told the woman that her bank cards were required as they were investigating a fraud The conman said it was suspected people working for her bank were involved in the fraud which is why they required her cards. An accomplice, acting as a courier was then sent to the woman's home in Macclesfield She handed over two debit cards and a credit card. But she later suspected she had been scammed and alerted police. Luckily the bank were able cancel her cards before the criminals could use them The case was one of five attempted courier frauds in eight days this month in Cheshire. All the victims were elderly. Aaron Law-Glindon, 28, split with the woman in February 2024, though they continued to live together at her home She was on civil terms with another ex-boyfriend, who was visiting one day the following September. Fortunately, the victim only needed stitches Law-Glindon was hauled before a judge this week for sentencing having previously admitted a charge of wounding. Recorder Imran Shafi KC told him: "Your actions that day were absolutely disgraceful. You behaved like an animal, which is doing a disservice to most animals." evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Warning notice issued for Greater Manchester hospital 'Excessively long waits' for beds saw one patient wait 44 hours Comments News Hannah Richardson 06:00, 17 Sep 2026 Updated 06:45, 17 Sep 2026 View 2 Images Accident and Emergency Department, An NHS trust has been issued a warning notice after concerns were raised over emergency services at a Greater Manchester hospital The Royal Albert Edward Infirmary, in Wigan , was found by inspectors to be among the worst in the country for the number of patients spending more than 12 hours in the emergency department. In the month prior to the inspection, 253 people had a wait of 12 hours or longer – an av This included ‘excessively long waits’ for speciality beds, with one patient waiting 44 hours during the inspection. There were ‘significant’ patient flow issues ‘across the hospital’, healthcare watchdog the Care Quality Commission added Additional delays were found at discharge with the trust again among the worst for this, the inspection report continued. Late paperwork meant some patients missed transport and care package cut-off times, in turn delaying discharge itself CQC inspectors reviewed two hospital services during their visit – Urgent and Emergency Services and Medical Care. Both received a rating of ‘requires improvement’, the second lowest of the four possible ratings – down from ‘good’ at their previous inspection

But they were woken up shortly after by a ‘loud crash’. Mr Marsden went to investigate and found a large fire in their rented end-of-terrace home in Bury He and his wife were able to escape the blaze, but their house was severely damaged and nine months on, remains uninhabitable. Their children had been staying elsewhere for the night Police recovered footage which showed Jody Lynam and a second, unknown offender approaching the house, at about 1.40am on January 18 this year. The unknown man smashed a window before Lynam poured petrol inside. An ‘explosion’ was caused and the pair fled Lynam was caught after DNA from a balaclava which he discarded nearby was traced to him. Comme An investigation is currently underway into why train services across the region were thrown into chaos last month . A new Bee Network report also said Avanti West Coast services were among the worst performing with cancellations doubling in July The new report, published ahead of a Bee Network committee meeting on September 24, said transport services ‘remained resilient during periods of extreme heat’. Despite the challenges , the report said it was ‘another good month’ for punctuality with both bus and Metrolink servic However rail services, which have not been taken over yet by Transport for Greater Manchester, performed worse. Problems faced included trespassing being ‘a major cause of disruption’ while crew availability continuing to be a problem All operators between June 28 to July 25 saw performance decline. Long distance operators saw the worst performance with only 42.7% of Avanti and 47% of CrossCountry trains running on time The report said Avanti was particularly hit with cancellations which more than doubled from 5.8 per cent to 12.1 pc. The tightknit neighbourhood jokingly describes itself as ‘a community of curtain-twitchers’. Really, it’s a place where people stop to chat on front porches, There’s just one major issue facing these neighbours: the recycling plant at the bottom of their road For years, residents claim they’ve been plagued by noise, bad smells, as well as rat and seagull infestations. The company, Fresh Start Waste, denies they are the source of any of these issues Earlier this month, the recycling site received planning permission from the council to erect a huge new outbuilding. Now the firm has put an application into the Environmental Health Agency to double the amount of waste it’s processing - from 75,000 tonnes to 150,000 tonnes View 8 Images The processing site on Hilton Square, backing onto Heron Street. One of the three remained inside the building after a door was smashed and a fire started There was a 'spontaneous explosion of light and flames', prosecutor Henry Blackshaw said. Lillia is 5 ft 5; of slim build; with brown hair and glasses. She was last seen wearing a black zip-up hooded top GMP's Major Incident Public Portal can be accessed HERE

Simon Richardson, 35, pleaded not guilty to murdering Mr Mullins. He died following an incident on April 20 this year Mr Richardson, of no fixed address, but formerly of Epsom Avenue in Sale, also pleaded not guilty to manslaughter and dangerous driving, by driving a Ford Transit van on roads including Williams Street, Oldham Road, Wellington Street, Peace Street, Wickentree Lane, Wrigley Head a He is due to go on trial next month at Minshull Street Crown Court. Emergency services were called to reports of a collision involving a car and a cyclist on Paddock Lane, in Dunham Massey near Altrincham, at around 6.10pm on April 20 The cyclist, Mr Mullins, 56, died at the scene. He had been headteacher of Stretford Grammar School for 17 years Judge Maurice Greene told Mr Richardson, who appeared in court by video link: “Your trial will be on October 13. There will be a pre-trial review, as things stand, on October 2. You will remain in custody.”

After gaining entry to the school hall, he claimed that somebody was after him and he thought he was 'going to be killed' During the seven minute fracas, Wallbank ran around various areas in the school, flipped a table and followed the headteacher into her office as she called 999. Whilst in her office he asked for help, telling her: "I've had a really bad trip, I need you to help me." He went on to smash a couple of windows within the school before fleeing to a neighbouring house. He was finally caught by police after climbing out of a window and falling from the ledge At Manchester Crown Court , a judge said: "I am told now you are terrified by the response you had and are deeply remorseful. I am sure that's cold comfort to the ladies subjected to you." Wallbank pleaded guilty to affray and criminal damage, and was today jailed for 20 months

The items were recovered by Greater Manchester Police before being passed on to Royal Mail Officers discovered the items after searching the property following an arrest in connection with a separate offence this summer, the Manchester Evening News understands. The number of items found was confirmed to be between 10,000 and 11,000 It's understood that the worker involved, who is believed to have been employed by Royal Mail in Bury for a number of years, is no longer with the business. Royal Mail has not confirmed whether the matter has been referred to police for a criminal investigation The M.E.N. understands each item of mail currently being held by Royal Mail will be delivered to its rightful recipient, along with a covering letter explaining the circumstances. Since being handed over to Royal Mail by police, the mail has been kept at the Bury delivery office, It has since been sorted by delivery area and is now being prepared for delivery, it is understood. Some of the items recovered are believed to have been damaged or tampered with in some way

She ended up becoming their head of accounts, and held sole responsibility for all the financial aspects of the company, Minshull Street Crown Court heard in February this year However, from 2008, she abused her position to steal from them in three 'discreet' ways; by claiming unauthorised overtime payments, stealing petty cash and unauthorised use of the company's credit card The total loss to the company was £128,352, the court heard. The fraud was revealed in June 2019 when it was discovered Clarke had been using the credit card. She claimed the fraud had been going on for six months, when in fact it had actually been taking place over 11 years An investigation revealed the full extent of Clarke's dishonesty. She pleaded guilty to three charges of fraud by abuse of position and was jailed for 18 months

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Trafford Old Trafford site to be turned into 286 homes with just seven parking spaces Old Trafford residents fear an 'influx of on-street parking' Comments News Hannah Richardson 13:21, 15 Sep 2026 View Image CGI of the proposed Chester Road flats, in Almost 300 new homes could be built on the site of a disused petrol station and multi-storey car park in Old Trafford . The scheme, recommended to be approved by Trafford council’s planning committee next week, would see the existing structures demolished and two blocks of 286 fl One of the blocks would reach 16-storeys in height and contain 192 homes. The second would have 94 flats and be six-storeys at its tallest point But concerns have been raised by residents over a lack of parking provision on the land, which sits off Chester Road. Just seven vehicle spaces are proposed, which would be disabled spaces. Some 286 cycle spaces would also be offered Residents have branded this offering ‘insufficient’, saying there is already a ‘lack of parking’ in the area. They fear the development would bring an ‘influx of on-street parking’ which could cause obstruction and poor visibility on the surrounding roads They have also raised concerns about illegal parking and traffic congestion. Trafford council would typically expect around 425 parking spaces to be delivered for a scheme of this size

He was serving a controversial indeterminate public protection sentence , having been jailed aged 17 for two-and-a-half years for attempted robbery The 32-year-old was released in 2022, having spent 13 years in prison, but was recalled the following year after failing a drugs test. On June 18 last year he was found hanged in his cell and died in Royal Oldham Hospital three days later Now Manchester North senior coroner Joanne Kearsley has raised urgent concerns about his death. In a prevention of future deaths report sent to the prison and the chief coroner Ms Kearsley wrote: "Upon finding Mr Hamer the prison officers did not cut the ligature for nearly three "It was heard that they panicked and were visibly distressed on finding Mr Hamer. They had undertaken their basic life support training years ago on their initial prison officer training."

The trio had been seen riding the mopeds near Tyldesley Old Road, in Atherton , on Tuesday evening (September 23) One of the men dropped a knife as he fled the scene. Officers carried out checks on the two mopeds, which confirmed the vehicles had been stolen. Greater Manchester Police says it is now working to identify the three people involved A GMP Wigan and Leigh spokesperson said: "Whilst on patrol this evening [Tuesday], neighbourhood officer PC Clarke disturbed three suspicious males riding mopeds near Tyldesley old Road. Then he got straight on his moped and did the very thing that landed him behind bars in the first place And the police were ready and waiting for him to do so. Between Southall Street and what is now the AO Arena the 59-year-old Sikh, known as Gyani Ji, was stopped and ticketed seven times His crime was refusing to remove his turban to wear a helmet while riding his 50cc Honda moped. And his small but persistent acts of civil disobedience would result in a landmark change in the law Gyani Ji was an activist who played a pivotal role in advancing Sikh religious rights in the UK. Born in Punjab, India, now Pakistan after partition, he moved to Manchester in 1948 and went on to help establish one of Europe's earliest Sikh temples in Moss Side His first high-profile campaign came in 1959 when he was denied a job as bus conductor due to uniform requirements which meant he would have to remove his turban and wear a cap. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Homelessness Rough sleeping rises in Greater Manchester as Andy Burnham pledges to end crisis by Christmas The number of rough sleepers across Greater Manchester went up in June, new figures show, as Prime Minister Andy Burnham vows to get every rough Comments News Paul Gallagher 05:57, 14 Sep 2026 The number of people sleeping rough across Greater Manchester has reached one of its highest levels in six years, according to new data released as former mayor Andy Burnham pledged to make homelessness a national priority Government data shows there were 444 rough sleepers across the ten boroughs of Greater Manchester in June 2026, up from 402 in June 2025 - a rise of 42 people, or 10.4 per cent. It is the highest figure for June, and the fourth highest monthly total since October 2020 The figures land as Mr Burnham - who made ending rough sleeping his first pledge on entering Downing Street in July - is pushing ahead with a national drive to get every rough sleeper off the streets by Christmas , backed by a £442 million funding package The biggest driver of the rise in Greater Manchester was Manchester city itself, where the number of rough sleepers in June jumped from 149 last summer to 195 - an increase of 46 people Tameside saw the second sharpest rise, climbing from 21 to 33, while Trafford rose from 6 to 10 and Bury edged up from 29 to 31. Not all boroughs saw increases. Salford , Oldham , Rochdale and Bolton recorded slightly lower numbers sleeping rough on their streets

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Salford mayor calls for city to unite following launch of murder investigation, HMO attack, removal of anti-migrant banners and reports of yobs terrorising suburb 'The spirit of Salford is what unites us' View 6 Images A house on Kingsley Aven Add to preferred sources News Ramazani Mwamba News reporter 18:25, 07 Oct 2026 Updated 20:12, 07 Oct 2026 Salford mayor Paul Dennett has called on the city to unite following 'high-profile incidents... that will have caused concern and anxiety in our communities' Mr Dennett issued a statement after a murder investigation was launched at a property in Lower Broughton ; an 'HMO' was trashed in Kersal ; roadside banners opposing 'migrant HMOs' were put up ; and reports of people being targeted by yobs hurling fireworks amid anti-social behav "Our city motto is 'the welfare of the people is the highest law'," Mr Dennett wrote. "Any attempt to divide people, spread hatred or target individuals because of who they are is completely unacceptable. The spirit of Salford is what unites us." It came as a murder investigation was launched after a man was found dead at a property on Great Clowes Street, Lower Broughton, on Wednesday (October 7). The Manchester Evening News understands the building at the centre of the murder probe is a house of multiple occupancy (HMO) Cops were called following the death of a man in his 40s on Tuesday (October 7). Greater Manchester Police said the man was found unresponsive inside the building

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Stalybridge man arrested at work after police make terrifying finds in raid on his home Jacob Naylor has been jailed after the discovery of 'significant threats' in his house News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 10:27, 01 Oct 2026 View 2 Images J A Tameside man with a 'fascination' with firearms has been jailed for five years after police found a viable 3D-printed semi-automatic pistol at his home. Officers from the North West Regional Organised Crime Unit swooped on the home of Jacob Naylor, of Huddersfield Road in Staly In a search warrant they seized two 3D printed firearms, plastic and metal firearms parts, 9mm rounds and a 3D printer, as well as a bag of cannabis Together with the Metropolitan Police’s Forensic Firearms Unit, the force established that the two firearms were a FGC-9 and a 'DIY' AR9 made from plastic and metal pressured parts. The 9mm were not live rounds The AR9 was found to be missing some components and was not useable, but the FGC-9 was found to be capable of firing bullets and being used as a firearm Naylor's DNA was found on both the printer and the firearms, with instructions and codes detailing how to manufacture and assemble the firearms found on the printer SD card

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police His stark grave says 'you didn't deserve to go this way' - now GMP are reinvestigating his murder Coroner calls for police review into the death of 43-year-old found in undergrowth after witnesses claim a 'conspiracy of silen Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 05:52, 15 Sep 2026 Updated 06:24, 15 Sep 2026 A week before Christmas in 2024 his family and friends gathered at the Raka Raka bar and restaurant in Salford . The venue on Cottenham Lane lies in the middle of a sprawl of industrial units It specialises in Zimbabwean and Southern African cuisine - flame -grilled meats, Boerewors traditional sausage, and staple foods like sadza from ground maize. The bar has imported beer like Hunters Dry and DJs play Afrobeat But the mood was respectful and reflective. Those present were remembering one of their own, Tanyaradzwa Julius Matera The next day, on December 18, many of them also attended his funeral at Peel Green Cemetery chapel followed by burial nearby in a tree-lined plot. His final resting place is more than 5,000 miles from his homeland A simple grey cross marks his grave and on the plaque bearing his name is embossed with: "You didn't deserve to go this way. Rest in Peace"

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Stockport Stockport care home boss says 'I didn't think a human could fit through' after gran falls to death from bedroom window The inquest into the death of 78-year-old Maureen O'Callaghan is being heard at Stockport Coroners' Court View 2 Images Ma News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 06:10, 18 Sep 2026 The former manager of a care home where a beloved gran fell to her death from her bedroom window - having previously attempted to climb through - told an inquest he did not believe a 'human being could fit through' Maureen O'Callaghan, who had dementia, died at Berrycroft Manor in Romiley, Stockport, on September 29 last year. The 78-year-old fell through her upstairs bedroom window, having previously attempted to climb out and throwing items from it Ms O'Callaghan's loved ones have told an inquest into her death, being heard at Stockport Coroners' Court, they believe her death was a 'preventable tragedy' Coroner Jyoti Gillearlier earlier heard Ms O'Callaghan moved to Berrycroft Manor in January 2025 to benefit from '24-hour care' at a cost of '£1,600 a week'. Her family said they had spoken to care home staff with safety concerns about the window, but nothing was done about Describing Ms O'Callaghan's death as a 'preventable tragedy', the family said: "She was an integral part of our close family and her loss will stay with us all."

Officers from Greater Manchester Police and West Midlands Police carried out two raids in Wolverhampton on Wednesday morning (October 7) As well as the arrests, the operation led to the discovery of large quantities of illegal drugs, stolen vehicles and cash The search of an address on Penn Road saw a man in his 60s arrested on suspicion of conspiracy to supply controlled drugs, he remains in police custody. Officers also seized approximately £1,000 in cash and around 50 Class C tablets At the second address on Stephen Close, a teenager was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of controlled drugs and theft of a motor vehicle. A woman in her 40s was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of controlled drugs and child endangerment The pair remain in custody. Co-defendant Mario-Alexandru Ratoiu, 26, pleaded guilty to engaging in sexual activity with a child, having previously been charged with rape Prosecutors told Manchester Crown Court Mario-Alexandru Ratoiu's plea to the less serious charge was acceptable. Both men, of no fixed address, are due to be sentenced at the same court in December The charges came after police received a report of a rape at a flat in the Green Quarter area of the city in April. The defendants, both Romanian nationals, were arrested and remanded in custody, where they remain The full circumstances of the case have not yet been outlined in open court. They entered guilty pleas ahead of a proposed trial, which was due to start today (October 6)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Northern 'Unreliable' Northern trains could be a thing of the past if Greater Manchester gets its way If the UK Government hands out the cash needed, up to 450 new trains could be running on train tracks across the region. Comments News Edward Barnes Northern Rail’s ‘ageing’ and ‘unreliable’ trains could soon be a thing of the past if Manchester transport bosses get their way Northern is currently bidding for funding which would see the rail operator’s largest ever investment in its fleet. If the UK Government hands out the cash needed, up to 450 new trains could be running on train tracks across the region If approved, the new trains would be introduced on a phased basis, replacing the oldest units in the fleet, most of which have been in service since the 1980s and 90s. Approximately two thirds of the existing fleet is targeted to be replaced in the next ten years According to Northern’s website, they hope to award contracts in 2027 with the first trains delivered by 2030. A total of 130 new trains would be delivered as part of phase one over three years replacing trains at or near ‘the end of their life’ An update was given on the major investment plan at a recent Bee Network committee meeting following questions on transport issues across Greater Manchester

Emergency services were called out to Atherleigh Way at 4.02pm on Monday, September 14 Greater Manchester Police says a man and a woman, both in their 80s, suffered serious injuries following the collision. They were inside a white Kia Soul, which is believed to have veered across the carriageway and into a silver Hyundai Tucson In an update issued today (September 23), GMP said the woman - who was a passenger in the Kia - has since sadly died from her injuries. The crash is being investigated by GMP's Serious Collision Investigation Unit Witnesses are now being urged to come forward with any information that could assist the investigation. Anyone with relevant CCTV, dashcam, doorbell or mobile phone footage from the area is also asked to contact police Details can be passed on to GMP by calling 0161 856 4741 or using the online Live Chat service, quoting log number 2521 of September 14, 2026. Alternatively, contact the independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111
